name: AeroSpace window ids
description: Window identity for tile: private _AXUIElementGetWindow(AXUIElementRef, *mut u32) -> AXError (AeroSpace Sources/PrivateApi/include/private.h) gives the CGWindowID; an error or kCGNullWindowID means not a window (drop it, e.g. Finder desktop). CGWindowIDs belong to the window server, so they stay valid across a Flick restart and a screen lock. Native macOS tabs swap the CGWindowID of the visible tab: when one id disappears and one appears in the same app in one refresh, keep the tree slot (AeroSpace MacApp.swift:376-388). AeroSpace is MIT (commit bc6be84): code may be copied with its notice.

Hiding windows without native Spaces: macOS clamps a window moved fully off-screen back on screen, so tile parks it with its top-left 1px inside a bottom corner of its screen's visible rect (bottom-right x=maxX-1,y=maxY-1; bottom-left x=minX+1-width; pick the corner that touches fewer other monitors). Only position is set, size kept. AeroSpace restores parked windows ONLY from its menu Quit; after SIGTERM, kill -9 or a crash they stay in the corners.
resolution: Store each hidden window's frame (module store table) before hiding, restore all in app::on_terminate + quit_on_sigterm, and on Started move back any window parked at a hide corner (saved frame, else centred on its nearest screen). Exit test for any change to hiding: kill -9 Flick while a workspace is hidden; every window must come back on relaunch.

title: Per-app AX threads, no messaging timeout
rationale: AX calls are synchronous IPC into the target app; one beachballed app on a shared thread (or the main thread) stalls every frame set. AeroSpace runs one CFRunLoop thread per app (MacApp.swift:67-98), never sets AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout, sends frame sets fire-and-forget with a newer set cancelling a pending one, turns the app's AXEnhancedUserInterface off around each set (big speedup), sets size-position-size, and on a workspace switch shows the target's windows before hiding the old ones. AX observers for every app: app WindowCreated/FocusedWindowChanged/MainWindowChanged, window UIElementDestroyed/Miniaturized/Deminiaturized/Moved/Resized, plus a leftMouseUp monitor because Destroyed is unreliable. AX elements stay on their app thread; the main thread gets plain data.

title: Tile prefix and resize modes use transient Carbon hotkeys, not the key tap
rationale: AeroSpace binds its modes with Carbon hotkeys (HotKey lib, config/Mode.swift). Carbon hotkeys still fire under secure input, where Flick's key tap sees no key down/up (flick-1271), and keeping them out of the tap leaves 'only keys uses the tap' true. The layer swaps out always-on bindings with the same spec (Hyper+h focus vs prefix Hyper+h swap) while armed.
